title: tooling(pin): register the seven ported hook files, each at its own upstream ref
body:
Fixes #8696

Registers the seven remaining ported `.claude/hooks/**` files in `scripts/upstream-port-pin.json`, **per file** rather than as one batch. All seven took outcome (A) — registered at their own `ref`, with every difference declared as an exact text pair carrying a one-sentence `why`. None needed outcome (B), so there is no "not pinned, because …" row below.

⛔ No `.claude/**` byte moves: `--resync` was never run, `--rewrite-governed-file` was never passed, and the pin schema is untouched. The diff is the ledger file plus a changeset.

## Per-file outcome

Ref column shows the short sha; each entry carries the full 40-character sha, as `validatePin` requires. "pairs" is the declared divergence count for that entry. The last column is what the same measurement gives at upstream `origin/main` today (`c2520416c` blob for every one of these paths), which is the alternative ref considered.

| ported file | upstream ref | outcome | pairs | why, in one line | at upstream main instead |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout.sh` | `c2520416c` | registered | 2 | card requalification (objectui#7259 for upstream's #11809) and the dropped note about a numbered Prime Directive this repo's AGENTS.md does not have | same ref — this IS upstream main's blob |
| `.claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout-bash.sh` | `924f0fed1` | registered | 21 | objectui paths and package names, upstream card numbers qualified with their repo, sibling-anchored framing, and the same missing-PD-number note | 22 pairs |
| `.claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout-bash.selftest.sh` | `924f0fed1` | registered | 10 | specimen paths and package names this repo has, plus the same card requalification in the case headers | 12 pairs |
| `.claude/hooks/guard-shared-stash.sh` | `2b9f5810b` | registered | 10 | this repo is the ORIGIN of this hook, so the provenance paragraph runs the other way; plus its own self-test case-count note and three regions of upstream prose this copy has not taken | 11 pairs |
| `.claude/hooks/guard-shared-stash.selftest.sh` | `2b9f5810b` | registered | 17 | two repos each wrote their own twin of the backslash fix, so the pairs are between two versions of one section, plus the usual specimen localisation | 19 pairs |
| `.claude/hooks/guard-tree-enum.sh` | `c074c57e4` | registered | 3 | the measured incident is THIS repository's, so the prose reads in the first person, and the mirroring note points the other way | 4 pairs |
| `.claude/hooks/guard-tree-enum.selftest.sh` | `c074c57e4` | registered | 6 | same first-person framing plus specimen paths, scripts and packages this repo actually has | 8 pairs |

objectui#7953's blocker is gone as the card says: two of these (`guard-tree-enum.sh` and its self-test) did not exist upstream at the ledger-wide ref that card was measured against, and they are now pinned at `c074c57e4`, the commit that created them upstream.

## How the ref was chosen, per file

The rule applied, stated so it can be argued with rather than inferred: **take the newest upstream ref whose content this copy already tracks.** A ref newer than that adds pairs that are upstream work this repo has not ported; a ref older than that adds pairs that hide upstream work this copy already has. Both directions were measured; the last table column is the newer-ref side of that measurement.

The operational reason the newest-ref default was not taken blindly: `--resync` applies the declared pairs FORWARD onto the new upstream text. A pair that declares "upstream has a paragraph we do not" therefore teaches every future re-sync to delete that paragraph again, permanently. At the chosen ref those regions are simply not pairs, and a later re-sync brings them across.

The rule also moves the other way, and did for one file. `guard-shared-stash.selftest.sh` reaches its smallest set (7 pairs) at `9f2280163`, but that ref predates a fix this copy HAS — the whole backslash matrix collapses into one 39-line pair that reads as objectui-only work and hides the fact that upstream has an equivalent. `2b9f5810b` costs 10 more pairs and is the honest one: there the pairs are between two versions of the same section, including the case-matrix rows each repo carries and the other does not.

For `guard-main-checkout.sh` the rule lands on upstream `origin/main`'s own blob, and that entry has 2 pairs and zero executable lines.

## Verdict lines, before and after

`origin/main` `e7173d9db`, `node scripts/check-upstream-port-parity.mjs`, exit 0:

```
✓ check-upstream-port-parity: 4 ported file(s) match objectstack-ai/objectstack modulo their declared divergences, each at its own pinned ref (3 distinct: bf10debd5, 70e77ec3b, 61362932b). (The digest is verified; the ref beside it is provenance and is NOT fetched.)
```

This branch, same command, exit 0:

```
✓ check-upstream-port-parity: 11 ported file(s) match objectstack-ai/objectstack modulo their declared divergences, each at its own pinned ref (7 distinct: bf10debd5, 70e77ec3b, 61362932b, c2520416c, 924f0fed1, 2b9f5810b, c074c57e4). (The digest is verified; the ref beside it is provenance and is NOT fetched.)
```

Every one of the seven new entries prints its own `✓ … byte-identical to objectstack-ai/objectstack@REF:PATH modulo N declared divergence(s).` line.

The gate's self-test, run first as `lint.yml` runs it, exit 0: `✓ check-upstream-port-parity self-test: 58 cases pass — …`.

## What the new entries make visible

The point of a ledger row is that it can be read. Three of the new pairs say out loud that this copy is behind upstream, and they are labelled that way in their `why` rather than dressed as decisions:

- `guard-shared-stash.sh` — upstream's recovery-by-scrollback paragraph, and the fourth alternative in both the header list and the printed remedy (commit the fix first, then take it out with a path-scoped checkout).
- `guard-shared-stash.selftest.sh` — upstream's `&&` twin and its `git -C` twin of the escaped-quote block case.

Acting on those means editing `.claude/**`, which this card forbids; they are now ledger rows instead of nothing.

## Acceptance notes

Out-of-scope observations, noted rather than filed (neither is a reproducible defect, a declared-contract breach, nor a metadata trap):

- `.github/workflows/lint.yml` line 307 still reads "Ported from objectstack `scripts/check-bash32-floor.mjs` … and deliberately NOT registered in `scripts/upstream-port-pin.json` — that ledger carries ONE global `upstream.ref`". Both halves have been false since objectui#8288 retired the field and objectui#8694 registered the file; objectui#8694 remains open as the card whose PR left the comment behind.
- `scripts/check-bash32-floor.mjs`'s "## Why this port is not YET pinned" section says "It is still NOT registered". Same staleness, same taker; that file is itself a pinned port, so repairing it is a divergence-declaring edit rather than a free one.

Neither is touched here: this PR's diff is the ledger plus a changeset, and widening it would put a governed-adjacent workflow edit into a PR whose whole claim is that it moved no ported byte.

## Local verification

- `node scripts/check-upstream-port-parity.mjs --self-test` → exit 0, 58 cases.
- `node scripts/check-upstream-port-parity.mjs` → exit 0, 11 of 11 green.

- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` → exit 0; `node scripts/check-changeset-claims.mjs` → exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on both changed paths → `NOT GOVERNED`, 2 paths against 5 surfaces.
- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/upstream-port-parity-wiring.test.ts` → `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 12 passed (12)`. This is the gate's own wiring suite and the only suite in the tree that reads the pin file; it asserts coverage, the per-entry `ref`, and that no pinned path falls inside `lint.yml`'s ignore set — the last one being what a new entry could have broken.

All of the above were run on `7394d3df7`, this branch's head after the final commit, against a clean working tree. The repo-wide farm is CI's run, not this seat's.
